body:
Add optional CPU acceleration for Torch search workloads.

## Standard information about the request

This is a: optional CPU efficiency update.

This change affects: Torch search kernels and CPU FFT dispatch.

This change: retains the two optional Cython feature additions, guarded dispatch and focused regressions; separate native-build and test receipts are linked below.

This change changes: optional native kernels and Torch CPU FFT dispatch.

This change will: require rebuilding the optional native extensions when enabling these routes.

## Motivation

Search workloads repeatedly compute batch peaks, sparse chi-square values and CPU FFTs; optional routes allow those costs to be optimized with explicit eligibility checks.

## Contents

Native batched peak and single-point chi-square kernels, guarded dispatch, and CPU FFT thread/plan tuning. This branch contains the two Cython additions excluded from the main stack and includes focused tuning and invalidation tests.

Preserve the existing optional Cython feature additions and their dispatch gate. Torch CPU FFT tuning keeps direct plans at power-of-two sizes from 32768 through 524288 samples; the large promoted workspace is limited to one thread. Other thread counts retain fallback behavior. Inherited main-stack improvements remain outside this PR’s feature diff.

The native CPU batch-peak flag and expanded direct-plan range belong to this optional leaf. Its pre-existing general CPU/native changes remain outside the main conversion and its scientific qualification.

## Links to any issues or associated PRs

Depends on [#15](https://github.com/xangma/pycbc/pull/15). Optional leaf; separate from main-stack scientific qualification. PR #20 is withdrawn from this stack.

Base: `torch-pr11-performance-evidence`. Head: `torch-followup-cpu-optimizations` at `95ed021935cdae7803f74715e4591333f11b5ce4`.

Unchanged original CPU reference: `40e94792b3edf59f39b18b65102b28a4f74433a7`.

[Campaign and test evidence](https://github.com/xangma/pycbc/tree/31039e44d35ece9c6d755bd265c854d2bd8bb6a6/original-cpu-restoration); [tested-source mapping and documentation checks](https://github.com/xangma/pycbc/tree/a5d237cb4f4ed7a4e26d6b8ffa4aa0c1fc7b2964/original-cpu-restoration/final-publication).

## Testing performed

Separate optional-leaf validation: **627 passed, 102 skipped**, with native-build provenance. These regression results do not establish full-search scientific equivalence for this optional leaf.

Completed main-stack campaign at `aa6b795a63bb18c4e63e4f4c203ca6e7c039d0f0` (separate from this optional leaf's validation): **CPU preservation PASS, 1988 = 1988 triggers**; all 18 scientific H1 datasets and full PSD arrays are byte-identical, with matching geometry. Conditioned-strain identity is verified by full-data SHA256 and metadata; raw conditioned strain was not archived.

**Torch CPU and Torch CUDA: 1991 triggers each, FAIL** against both CPU controls under unchanged trigger/full-PSD gates. Only four recorded runtime/timing fields are excluded; raw and corrected verdicts are retained. No performance samples or speedup claim.
